newsitem.title: USA: US House panel following Senate derivatives debate.
newsitem.headline: US House panel following Senate derivatives debate.

text.p: House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach said Monday he is following developments in the Senate Agriculture Committee concerning regulation of futures and derivatives trading.
Asked by a reporter if his committee would take an interest in the issue or hold hearings, Leach said "absolutely." But the Iowa Republican added a caveat that "we've made no firm decisions."
A bill introduced in the Senate would streamline some existing futures trading regulations and allow off-exchange trading of some futures by certain institutional investors.
"It is very important that they (the issues) be looked at from the point of view of the public interest as contrasted with committee rivalries," Leach noted.

The Senate bill would also clarify a murky section of existing law on foreign exchange trading. Known as the Treasury Amendment to the Commodity Exchange Act, the 1974 law exempts most forex trading from the jurisdiction of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
Fed chairman Alan Greenspan said last week that Congress should be careful not to overregulate derivatives trading while clarifying the amendment.

Off-exchange derivatives trading by institutions should not be subject to CFTC rules, Greenspan said. CFTC oversight is likely not needed for off-exchange trading by retail investors with banks and broker-dealers that are already federally supervised, he added.

Leach told reporters that while he is unsure if the House Banking Committee will take any action on the matters being considered by the Senate, "as a general rule, I tilt to the judgement of the Fed on issues of this nature."
